explanation: Tipton dissent (not the majority) cites Sainz in 1980 as showing New Mexico decides entrapment objectively as a matter of law; Fiechter (1976) overruled Sainz on exactly that government-conduct focus; no negative history noted; unrelated Illinois case.

citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit
explanation: Von Hofe quotes Grady only for the general maxim that a problem's severity cannot excuse adherence to constitutional principles; Dixon overruled Grady's same-conduct double jeopardy test, a different point, so limb 1 fails.

McNair cites Schuessler for the point that mental disease does not itself establish legal insanity; Meraz overruled Schuessler only on the appellate standard for reviewing affirmative-defense findings, a different point.

citing_name: Gray v. Department of Social Services
citing_court: United States District Court for the Southern District of New York
explanation: Gray cites Collins for no entitlement to a decision-maker of one's own race; Brooks disapproved Collins's holding that purposeful inclusion of Negroes invalidates an indictment, and itself reaffirmed that proportional representation is not required; different point.

Julien quotes Bourque (through Wells) only for deference to trial-court credibility findings; Comeaux overruled Bourque's limit on penalty-phase evidence of unadjudicated crimes, an unrelated point, so limb 1 fails.

citing_name: Auclair v. American Silk Spinning Co.
explanation: Tulsa Hotel disapproved Dunkelberger's latent-injury limitations rule, but Auclair only recites it as the employee's argument (noting an earlier Rhode Island quotation) and decides on its own statute's knew-or-should-have-known text; no reliance.

citing_name: W. P. Brown & Sons Lumber Co. v. Burnet
citing_court: Supreme Court of the United States
explanation: Brown footnote lists Reliance among Board decisions holding section 283(f) confirmed Board jurisdiction; Art Metal overruled Reliance on whether collection was time-barred under the 1921/1924 Acts, a different point, so limb 1 fails.

French cites Alford only for four-corners intent and harmonizing all parts of a deed; Luckel overruled Alford's granting-clause-controls holding and itself endorses the four-corners/harmonizing rule, so the negation is on a different point.

citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit
explanation: Second Circuit cites Lee for ordinary emotional or financial tribulations of family separation not being extreme hardship; Wang overruled Lee only insofar as inconsistent (prima facie showing, combined hardships) and itself says economic detriment alone is insufficient.

citing_court: United States District Court for the District of Montana
explanation: District court quotes Hammer as authority that the Tenth Amendment reserves local matters from Congress and strikes down a federal statute; Darby overruled Hammer and rejected that reasoning in 1941; no mention of Darby or the overruling.

Woods cites Walton II for abuse-of-discretion review of leave to amend; the 2007 Supreme Court decision reversed the later trial judgment on law-of-the-case grounds, not Walton II or its amendment standard, per the excerpt.

citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit
explanation: Betts appears only in Judge Wellford's separate opinion, as the source Screws quoted on due process being a fluid concept; it is description of Screws, not reliance on Betts's right-to-counsel holding that Gideon overruled.

citing_name: PS Chez Sidney, L.L.C. v. United States International Trade Commission
citing_court: United States Court of International Trade
explanation: Whitney appears only inside a block quotation from New York Times v. Sullivan citing Brandeis's concurrence on free discussion; Brandenburg overruled the Whitney majority's syndicalism holding, not that concurrence, and the court relies on Sullivan.

Valleylab cites Ex parte Slade in a string cite for the mandamus prerequisites; Creel overruled only Slade's portion on probate-court jurisdiction over common-law marriage and itself restates the same mandamus standard.

Johnson never cites McEwen; it cites Smith v. State, 302 Ark. 459 (sharing a S.W.2d page cite) for the directed-verdict standard. Sutton overruled McEwen only on felon/firearm joinder prejudice, a different point.

citing_name: Welch v. City of Lincoln Park
explanation: Welch cites Kavanaugh v. Baird only on res judicata/lack of identity of parties. Hilt overruled it on Great Lakes title between meander line and water, a different proposition; negation not on point.

Yurina cites Anderson for no double jeopardy in using priors both as aggravator and habitual enhancement. Rhyne overruled Anderson only on imposing a separate habitual sentence rather than enhancing a felony sentence; different point.

Joy relies on Green only for conviction on uncorroborated accomplice testimony, which Turner reaffirmed. Turner disapproved only the cautionary-scrutiny statement, which Joy recites as defendant's argument and declines to apply.

South Carolina court twice cites the Arizona Court of Appeals Camargo opinion as authority that independent verification/controlled buy shows informant reliability, though the Arizona Supreme Court vacated that opinion outright in 1975; no history noted; unrelated litigation.

cited_name: Klasing v. Fred Schmitt Contracting Co.
explanation: Slider cites Klasing (see also, p. 732) for employee procuring own medical treatment when employer neglects to furnish it. Mills overruled Klasing on construing the $3,600 average-annual-earnings exclusion; different point.

Sims quotes The Harrisburg, via Western Loan, for a statutory time limit conditioning the right itself. Moragne overruled only the holding that general maritime law gives no wrongful-death action; that limitation principle was untouched.

citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit
explanation: Ramirez cites Kahn (via Mendoza) for the joint-participation exception to marital privilege; the Supreme Court reversed only the 'others as yet unknown' wiretap ruling and did not review the privilege holding, so negation is on a different point.

Loudon quotes Gobitis as the Court's statement that religious scruples do not excuse obedience to general laws; Barnette overruled Gobitis outright in 1943, and the opinion nowhere notes that or cites Barnette.

Waters follows the 2003 Hill dismissal for non-compliance with Rule 24.3(b); the 2005 supreme court decision reversed a later court of appeals ruling in Hill's second appeal and cited the 2003 dismissal only as history, leaving it intact.

citing_name: Weisman v. Blue Shield of California
citing_court: Court of Appeal of the State of California
explanation: Weisman merely notes in a footnote that Roth (at 682) adopted conscious disregard as malice; Templeton disapproved Roth only on remittitur waiver of appeal (at 680), a different point, and the mention is historical.

Tindel cites Smith for a 'guilty' plea to enhancement equalling 'true'; Hill overruled Smith only to the extent it let an unobjected-to prior conviction be attacked by habeas alongside direct appeal, a different point.

citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit
explanation: Thomas relies on the Fourth Circuit's MacDonald rehearing decision for a speedy-trial Barker threshold point; the Supreme Court had reversed that Fourth Circuit speedy-trial judgment outright in 1982, and Thomas gives no subsequent history. Unrelated litigation.

Lukas cites Stein at 196 for hearsay admission not raising a constitutional question; Jackson v. Denno overruled Stein on the jury procedure for determining confession voluntariness, not that hearsay point (own knowledge: page 196 concerns hearsay/confrontation).
Veon quotes MCI WorldCom citing Harris only for the constitutional-avoidance canon; Alleyne overruled Harris's Sixth Amendment mandatory-minimum holding, a different point, so limb 1 fails.

citing_name: Daniel v. Southern Pacific Transportation Co.
explanation: Daniel cites Wiley for presuming unfurnished jury instructions adequately covered a requested concept; Wiley was overruled only on its Swain peremptory-challenge rule, so the negation is off point.

citing_court: United States Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Wisconsin
explanation: Bankruptcy court quotes Sinclair for the generic rule that courts give effect to discernible congressional intent; Boys Markets overruled Sinclair's Norris-LaGuardia injunction holding, not that general interpretive principle.
Fort relies on Rodriguez for the $5-a-day presentence credit against the drug assessment; Dexter overruled Rodriguez only on whether a private parking lot is a public way.

citing_name: Roberts v. American Family Mutual Insurance Co.
explanation: Only the dissent cites the 1980 Ward decision (Cf., issue not raised by parties); the 1985 Supreme Court ruling reversed the later 1983 court of appeals decision, not the 1980 one.

Stays quotes West citing Jarowecki for weight of evidence being the factfinder's choice; the Supreme Court reversal addressed only the second-offense grading question on limited review, leaving that point untouched.

cited_name: National League of Cities v. Usery
explanation: Texas Supreme Court applies National League of Cities and its Hodel traditional-governmental-functions test as the governing Tenth Amendment limit on commerce power; Garcia overruled exactly that in 1985, and Garcia is never mentioned.

citing_name: Ben Cheeseman Realty Co. v. Thompson
explanation: Parker overruled Lodge only on sufficiency of land description in a pleading tested by demurrer, saying its rule suits contracts. Cheeseman cites Lodge for certainty of description in a contract, a point not negated.

citing_name: Hans Hagen Homes, Inc. v. City of Minnetrista
cited_name: Alberte v. Anew Health Care Services, Inc.
explanation: Hans Hagen never cites Alberte; 588 N.W.2d 298 appears only as a mistaken reporter cite for Manco (583 N.W.2d 293), a Minnesota zoning case. No reliance on the reversed Wisconsin decision for any proposition.

cited_name: Krauss v. Utah State Department of Transportation
explanation: Krauss appears only inside a block quotation from New Mexico's Hansen opinion cataloguing intent-rule jurisdictions. The Kansas court surveys approaches and rests on Kansas cases (Geier, Stueve); it does not use Krauss as authority.

citing_name: Weidenhaft v. Shoppers Fair of Des Moines, Inc.
explanation: Iowa court string-cites Gill as supporting authority that plaintiffs are denied recovery for falls on floors wet from tracked-in rain, a year after Pribble overruled Gill on exactly that point; no mention of Pribble or the overruling.

Kott cites the N.C. Court of Appeals Hurst decision as support on inquiry into objections to appointed counsel, after the N.C. Supreme Court reversed that decision outright (on the larceny/robbery issue); no subsequent history given. Different litigation.

citing_name: Howard Hess Dental Laboratories Inc. v. Dentsply International, Inc.
citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit
explanation: Khan overruled Albrecht's per se rule against vertical maximum price fixing. The Third Circuit cites Albrecht at 150 n.6 only for the point that coerced acquiescence can still be a combination or agreement, which Khan did not disturb.

citing_name: Pelican Homestead & Savings Ass'n v. Winston
cited_name: League Central Credit Union v. Montgomery
explanation: Pelican relies on League Central, but the excerpted 30 Nov 1987 First Guaranty opinion applies League Central and affirms; from my knowledge the overruling came on rehearing in 1988, after Pelican (15 Dec 1987). Timing limb fails.

citing_name: Powers v. E.R. Precision Optical Corp.
explanation: Powers quotes Byrd citing Prahl for workplace robbery being an accident arising out of employment; Grace disapproved Prahl only on compensating mental injury without physical injury, a different point.

citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit
explanation: Proctor (1935) cites Inglish as supporting authority that an employee injured going home with work papers is in the course of employment; Gintert (1934) overruled Inglish on exactly that, and no mention is made.

Creekmore cites Moran alone for malice toward the owner being the gravamen of malicious mischief under section 1760; McDaris (1973) expressly overruled Moran on that element; no negative history noted.

Hausaman mentions the 147 Mo. App. 105 citation (as Purl's Estate) only as appellant's authority on estoppel and holds it inapplicable; Sage overruled Gupton on private-bank separate entity, a different point.

citing_court: United States District Court for the District of Maine
explanation: Iyamu relies on Barrett, which quotes Jackson's broad-interpretation maxim for requests for counsel; Montejo overruled Jackson's bar on police-initiated interrogation after arraignment request, not that maxim, and Barrett remains good law.

Coffey cites the Court of Appeals opinion for stating reasons for unequal property division; the Supreme Court on transfer addressed only child support review standard; from memory, remaining issues were summarily affirmed, so the point was not negated.

cited_name: Stein v. Asheville City Board of Education
explanation: Stacy cites and quotes the Court of Appeals' Stein opinion for no concurrent jurisdiction under 143-300.1 and 115C-42, though the Supreme Court had reversed that decision outright in 2006; no subsequent history is noted; different litigation.

citing_court: Luzerne County Court of Common Pleas
cited_name: Jacobs v. Board of School Commissioners
explanation: Court adopts Jacobs's reasoning on legal-services representation, but the excerpt shows no reversal; from my knowledge the Seventh Circuit affirmed. Only the 1975 Supreme Court mootness vacatur (420 U.S. 128) followed, not on this point.
